event.title: PPHM Open
event.description:
Pin Point Heritage Museum is open from Thursday – Saturday from 9am to 4pm.

Located in the former A.S. Varn & Son Oyster and Crab Factory, guests can discover the Gullah/Geechee culture and unique lifeways, from daily life to religion, language, and food directly from residents who grew up in the small, close-knit community.

event.title: SHM: Guided Programming
event.description: Savannah History Museum Guided Programs are held on Fridays and Saturdays at 10:30am, 12:00pm, and 2:00pm. Join us for family-friendly educational programming focusing on various topics of Savannah’s rich history. Interactive programming may be inside Savannah History Museum or continue outside on the adjacent Battlefield Memorial Park. Programs are included with your regular admission!

event.title: OFJ: Daily Programming and Cannon Firings
event.description: Join us for family-friendly educational programming focusing on the lives of soldiers once stationed at Fort Jackson and its 18th-century predecessor, Mud Fort! CHS Historical Interpreters will lead interactive programs on weaponry, wartime communications, military medicine, and more, while dressed as soldiers from different units present on-site over the 250 years of its history.

event.title: PPHM Open
event.description:
Pin Point Heritage Museum is open from Thursday – Saturday from 9am to 4pm.

Located in the former A.S. Varn & Son Oyster and Crab Factory, guests can discover the Gullah/Geechee culture and unique lifeways, from daily life to religion, language, and food directly from residents who grew up in the small, close-knit community.

event.title: Penguin Project Informational Meeting
event.description:
@

We are embarking on a very special endeavor! The Penguin Project is for special needs artists (ages roughly 10-25) to work on a theatrical production (Honk Jr.) with the aid of a mentor (ages roughly 12-25). This is a national project, and BST will be the first theatre in Montana to produce a Penguin Project show. Rehearsals will be twice a week starting in December (possibly more as we near show dates) . We will have informational meetings for artists and mentors (and their parents/guardians) at Lewis and Clark Middle School on Thursday October 1st, and Tuesday October 13th at 630 pm in the auditorium. Please enter through door #6 off of 14th Street West.
Honk Jr.
Honk Jr. tells the tale of Ugly. He looks quite a bit different from his darling duckling brothers and sisters. The other animals on the farm are quick to notice and point this out, despite his mother’s protective flapping. Feeling rather foul about himself, the little fowl finds himself on an adventure of self-discovery, all the while unknowingly outwitting a very hungry cat. Along the way, Ugly meets a whole flock of unique characters and finds out being different is not a bad thing to be.
SHOW DATES – April 23, 24, 25, 2027 (at Billings Skyview High School)

event.title: Dracula A Comedy of Terrors
event.description:
@

Comedy. Ever wondered what would happen if you took Bram Stoker’s legendary vampire tale and put it into a blender with Mel Brooks, Monty Python, and The 39 Steps? That’s just what happens in this lightning-fast, laugh-out-loud, 90-minute, gender-bending romp. When her sister Mina falls ill with a mysterious disease of the blood, Lucy Westfeldt and her fiancé, Jonathan Harker, enlist the help of famed female vampire hunter Doctor Jean Van Helsing. Their hunt for the dangerous and sexy Count Dracula abounds with clever wordplay and quick-change antics. A great show for the spooky season! Advisory – contains mature (yet juvenile) content and humor.

October 9, 10, 11*, 15, 16, 17, 18*

*Donates a matinee performance

Tickets on sale for season ticket holders – September 15

Tickets on sale for ALL and online – September 22

event.title: Billings Studio Theatre’s Penguin Project
event.description:
@

We are embarking on a very special project this year!  The Penguin Project is where special needs artists (ages roughly 10-23) work on a production with the aid of a mentor (along with the production team). So, every artist will be paired up with a mentor to help them through rehearsals and performances. This is a nationally known project, started by Dr. Andy Morgan in 2004. BST will be the first theatre in Montana to produce a Penguin Project show. We are producing Honk JR, which is the charming musical tale of the Ugly Duckling and their friends. The performances will be held at Skyview High School auditorium. It is called the Penguin Project because even though penguins can’t fly, their spirits still soar.  

Tickets on sale for ALL and online – March 30th

event.title: Navigating the Genderverse Workshop
event.description:
Navigating the Genderverse Workshop | TransVisible Montana

This presentation is created and facilitated by TransVisible Montana collective members with the intention of creating a “brave space” for folks to gain education regarding the challenges that misinformation and cisnormative systems create for transgender, non-binary, and Two-Spirit Montanans.

Participants will learn what support is helpful in overcoming challenges and will be engaged in activities and discussions that deepen their understanding and comfort with pronouns and their use in introductions.

Participants will explore gender as a part of the human experience that expands beyond the gender binary, and identify effective and ineffective allyship qualities.

Participants will have the opportunity to collect TransVisible Montana resources such as posters, stickers, cards, and handouts that will be helpful in the continued practice of their newly acquired knowledge and allyship skills.

Outcomes Include:

  • A broadened awareness & practice of contemporary, inclusive language.
  • Applicable skills & ideas for work, home, school & public environments.
  • Permission for liberation from the gender binary!

Bricks and Brothels Historic Tour

While most in Missoula are familiar with the name Mary Gleim or the brief history of Front Street, many of the district’s stories remain untold including Gleim’s and her businesses. Since its existence along the historic Mullan Road, Front Street has been dubbed with the title of Missoula’s ‘red light district’ implicating that district remained a place of vice, sin, and corruption influenced by the radical reformist religious movements of the late 19th century. However, violence and addiction found throughout the entirety of the American West remain only a sliver of the true story.

From 1889-1917, West Front and Main Streets became home to a vibrant ‘restricted’ community of working women, Chinese laborers, African American soldiers, and immigrants who built the environment we as Missoulians have come to love today. This tour discusses the district through the historical lenses of sex, race, class, and occupation in order to create a broader social understanding against the backdrop of the remaining built environment.

event.title: Much Ado About Murder
event.description:
By Pat Cook / Rich but rotten Carlton Larraby enjoyed punctuating the lives of his family with macabre little surprises. His latest joke is a Halloween party with everybody dressed as a character from Shakespeare. When the play begins, the bored guests have arrived and wait impatiently for their host to show up, unaware that he has been gruesomely bludgeoned to death in his study. Since this is an audience-participation play, the murder is revealed to the audience before the characters of the play know about it. A sinister master of ceremonies named Mr. Hawker tells the audience what has happened in a series of flashbacks as he lets them see the events surrounding the murder. Little by little, as the audience gets to know the people of the drama, they begin suspecting who the murderer might be … only to discover that they’re wrong. To help them further, Mr. Hawker invites them to view the clue-rich scene of the crime during intermission. Finally, near the end of Act II, he gives the audience the opportunity to question the characters. All the ingredients of a deliciously frightening murder mystery are here—lightning, thunder, weird sounds, screams in the dark—plus the fun of letting the audience participate in solving the crime. As a critic pointed out, Much Ado About Murder provides a “whimsically entertaining night.”

event.title: Dashing Through The Snow
event.description:
By Jones/Hope/Wooten / It’s four days before Christmas in the tiny town of Tinsel, Texas, and a colorful parade of eccentric guests arrive at the Snowflake Inn, decking the halls with holiday hilarity. Trina, the harried yet upbeat innkeeper of this B&B, has more than she can handle coping with these nuttier-than-a-fruitcake lodgers. Hoyt and his sister, Donna Jo, make the mistake of trying to end a 30-year feud between their curmudgeonly aunts, with sidesplitting results. Ainsley and Lenora, self-involved actors from a lower-than-low-budget touring production of A Christmas Carol, descend on the inn to fulfill a promise, leaving comedic chaos in their wake. Add to this Yuletide mayhem an ill-advised romantic rendezvous between Mrs. Claus and one of Santa’s elves, a demanding guest who refuses to leave, not to mention a tipsy housekeeper, and it’s clear it will take more than a kiss under the mistletoe to keep Trina’s spirits merry and bright. But a spur-of-the-moment Christmas Eve wedding that brings together the fabulous Futrelle sisters and their best friend takes a surprising and delightful turn that leads to a laugh-’til-your-sides-ache climax, changing all their lives forever.

Learn about the history of Scouting during World War II.  Matthew Sedutto will give a talk about the overlooked role of Boy Scouts during World War II, when Scouts served in roles ranging from scrap drivers and messengers to civil defense volunteers.  Mr. Sedutto is an undergraduate honors student majoring in History at Norwich University.  He is also an Eagle Scout and volunteer at both the Wright Museum of World War II and the L. L. Lee Scouting Museum.

Come and learn about how scouts sold war bonds, collected scrap metal, and helped grow Victory Gardens. The talk highlights roles that New Hampshire’s Scouts played during that time, including New Hampshire’s little-known civilian messenger test, during which scouts carried messages by hand between Concord and Laconia, and how Scouts served as the official secretariat of the Bretton Woods Conference.  Part of the lecture will also examine the experiences of Japanese American scouts who continued participating in scouting while confined in wartime relocation camps. 

WHERE: Millyard Museum, 200 Bedford Street, Manchester
COST: Included with Regular Admission.  Scouts are free!

Learn more about the background of this project here: https://nhmuseumtrail.org/interns-passion-for-history-connects-two-nh-heritage-museum-trail-members/

event.title: America’s Pub Quiz Trivia Tuesdays
event.description:
Join us this and every Tuesday as we compete in a free and friendly game of trivia. Prizes awarded to the top 3 teams.

Join us this and every Tuesday as we compete in a free and friendly game of trivia. Prizes awarded to the top 3 teams.

America’s Pub Quiz is the best live-hosted trivia show that brings a free quiz night to bars, pubs, and restaurants throughout the United States. We are happy to bring fun trivia to family, friends and coworkers. An entertaining evening to be had by all guaranteed. We are so confident in your enjoyment that we aren’t going to charge you anything to play and provide free prizes!

Subject matter is a potpourri of categories, including music, movies, TV, sports, history, and more, with plenty of surprises along the way. A plethora of categories gives all team members their strong subject and ensures the useless knowledge stored away will finally be put to good use. Team size doesn’t matter and there are often prizes for the best team name or funniest wrong answer.

Grab your friends, invite that smart guy from the office, and come take a break with some great food & drink at one of America’s premier establishments. We promise, once you play along with America’s Pub Quiz, you’ll be back!

Prepare to explore the universe through music! Join the San Juan Symphony’s own Maestro Thomas Heuser for Musically Speaking: The Planets and Beyond, an engaging lecture that takes audiences behind the music of our Season 41 opener.

Discover the stories, ideas, and musical inspiration behind Gustav Holst’s iconic The Planets, along with John Adams’ thrilling Short Ride in a Fast Machine and Mélanie Bonis’ evocative Le Songe de Cléopâtre. Community Concert Hall, Durango

SJS Chamber Singers, Amy Barrett, director

San Juan Symphony

Thomas Heuser, conductor

    John Adams, Short Ride in a Fast Machine

    Mélanie Bonis, Le Songe de Cléopâtre, Op. 165

    Gustav Holst, The Planets (1914-1916)

Fasten your seatbelts for a concert of epic proportions! American composer John Adams slings the orchestra into high gear with his brilliant Short Ride in a Fast Machine, which propels us into Gustav Holst’s The Planets – a grand tour of the solar system. From Jupiter the Bringer of Jollity to Mars the Warrior and the wonderfully abstract Neptune, the music depicts Holst’s unique interpretations of each larger-than-life astrological character. Maestro Heuser and the San Juan Symphony will be joined by members of the SJS Chamber Singers and the Durango Women’s Chorus for this impactful musical experience. Our audiences will also be introduced to Mélanie Bonis, a rarely performed French avante-garde composer whose life and music are brimming with energy and drama. Her evocative tone poem, Le Songe de Cléopatre, is part of the huge orchestral triptych Trois Femmes de légende. Expect to be awash in incredible harmonies and the richness of this unusually massive orchestra.

event.description:
Musically Speaking: Romantic Giants

Wednesday, November 4, 2026

6pm-7pm

The Powerhouse (Durango)

This is a FREE event.

Light Snacks and Cash Bar available.

Step into the passionate world of Romantic-era music with the San Juan Symphony’s Musically Speaking: Romantic Giants. This engaging lecture with Maestro Heuser explores the stories, musical ideas, and larger-than-life emotions behind two masterpieces of the orchestral repertoire: Antonín Dvořák’s beloved Cello Concerto and Johannes Brahms’ powerful Symphony No. 3.

Learn more about these two towering composers, the expressive worlds they created, and the fascinating connections between their music before hearing these masterpieces performed live by the San Juan Symphony and cellist Tommy Mesa.

Whether you’re a longtime classical music fan or new to orchestral music, Musically Speaking offers an accessible and entertaining way to listen deeper and experience the concert from a whole new perspective.

6pm-7pm

Location TBD

This is a FREE event.

Discover the passion, power, and complexity behind the San Juan Symphony’s season finale, Iron and Ivory.. This engaging  lecture explores the emotional world of two giants of Russian music: Dmitri Shostakovich’s provocative Symphony No. 9 and Sergei Rachmaninoff’s sweeping and deeply expressive Piano Concerto No. 2.

Learn more about the fascinating stories behind these works, Shostakovich’s complicated response to the end of World War II, and the enduring appeal of Rachmaninoff’s beloved concerto. We’ll also take a closer look at guest pianist Norman Krieger, returning to the San Juan Symphony as featured soloist.

Come hear the stories behind the music and prepare for a powerful Season 41 finale filled with grandeur, emotion, and unforgettable orchestral sound.

event.title: New York State International Film Festival – October 2
event.description:
Join us October 2–3 at Steamer 10 Theatre for the 11th Annual New York State International Film Festival, a two-day celebration of independent filmmaking from around the world!

Doors open at 5:30 PM, with film screenings beginning at 6:00 PM each night. The festival will showcase a diverse selection of local, national, and international independent short films, bringing unique stories, creative voices, and talented filmmakers together for an exciting weekend of cinema.

In addition to the film screenings, audiences will have the opportunity to participate in Q&A panels with filmmakers, offering a behind-the-scenes look at the creative process and the stories behind the films.

The festival will also feature our Best Movies Award Ceremony, celebrating outstanding films and filmmakers selected from this year’s program.

We are proud to present the Brendan Fahy Bequette Fund Best Young Filmmaker Award, which includes a $500 cash prize to support and encourage the next generation of independent filmmakers.

Come experience two nights of great short films, meet filmmakers, participate in Q&A discussions, and celebrate independent cinema at the 11th Annual New York State International Film Festival!

event.description:
Lizzie Borden took an ax
And gave her mother forty whacks,
And when she saw what she had done,
She gave her father forty-one.

Steamer No.10 Theatre’s Eclectic Performance Series for Adult Audiences

presents the CAPITAL REGION PREMIERE OF

LIZZIE (The Musical)

Music by Steven Cheslik-DeMeyer and Alan Stevens Hewitt
Lyrics by Steven Cheslik-DeMeyer and Tim Maner
Book by Tim Maner
Additional Music by Tim Maner
Additional Lyrics by Alan Stevens Hewitt
Based on an original concept by Steven Cheslik-DeMeyer and Tim Maner
Orchestrations by Alan Stevens Hewitt

DIRECTED & CHOREOGRAPHED BY KELLY SIENKIEWICZ

ASSISTANT DIRECTED & STAGED MANAGED BY MELANIE MAGRI

MUSIC DIRECTED BY JESS FITZSISTI

 

STARRING…

MEGAN MORSE as EMMA

KELLY SIENKIEWICZ as BRIDGET

EMILY JENKINS as ALICE

REGAN ZLOTNICK as LIZZIE

MELANIE MAGRI as SWING

Rage! Sex! Betrayal! Bloody murder! In the heat of late summer 1892, Andrew Borden and his wife are found murdered in their house. The main suspect? Andrew’s youngest daughter from a previous marriage: Lizzie Borden. This all-woman musical sets American mythology to a searing rock score – complete with riffs on the historical record – to explore the heady and heated days leading up to the historical murder and Lizzie’s controversial acquittal of all charges.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

Prizes, Giveaways, & Bar Tabs for Winners!

Come for dinner. Stay for the fun. Win big at Bar Bingo!

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine

1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.

event.title: Boots, Buckles & Boogie
event.description:
Boots, Buckles & Boogie

Tuesday Country Nights at Seville Quarter

Welcome to Boss Phogg’s Honky-Tonk, where Tuesday nights are made for boots, buckles, and boogie!

Beginning Tuesday, October 6, Boots, Buckles & Boogie takes over Phineas Phogg’s at Seville Quarter with line dancing, partner dancing, Country Two-Step, Country Swing, and today’s hottest country music.

Dance instructor Dawn Alexander leads line and partner dance lessons from 7–9 p.m. Whether you are learning your first steps or fine-tuning your footwork, Dawn will have you boot-scootin’ with confidence in no time.

After the lessons, Honky-Tonk DJ Miss Janie takes over, playing country-dance favorites all night long on Boss Phogg’s dance floor.

With a true honky-tonk atmosphere andPensacola’s #1 dance floor, Phineas Phogg’s is the perfect place for beginners, experienced dancers, couples, singles, and groups of friends to gather, dance, and show off their moves.

The music will be playing, the crowd will be ready, and Boss Phogg’s dance floor will be calling your name!

event.title: Flip My Quarter
event.description:
Seville Quarter’s Flip My Quarter Happy Hour Just Got Even Better!

Every Friday | 6–8 PM | Seville Quarter

Downtown Pensacola’s hottest new Happy Hour is turning up the fun! After an incredible kickoff that packed the house, Seville Quarter is raising the stakes for Flip My Quarter, making it the can’t-miss Friday tradition.

Starting this week, you can flip your way into free drinks with an upgraded lineup, including:
Super Premium Cocktails
House Wine
Domestic Drafts & Bottled Beer

Here’s how it works:
1️⃣ Order one of the featured drinks.
2️⃣ Tell your bartender: “Flip My Quarter.”
3️⃣ Call it right when the Quarter’s in the air → Your drink is FREE!
4️⃣ Miss the call → You pay.

It’s that easy, and that fun. Add in live music, legendary Seville vibes, and the best crowd in town, and you’ve got the perfect way to kick off your weekend.

Tag your crew. Who’s feeling lucky? Join us this Friday and see if your drinks on the house!

event.title: Monday Night Blues
event.description:
Live Music Starts at 7:00 PM | Lili Marlene’s | Smoke-Free Venue

Seville Quarter and the Blues Society of Northwest Florida are proud to bring the Blues back to Downtown Pensacola, every Monday night in Lili Marlene’s!

Join us for Monday Night Blues Open Jam, a high-energy celebration of one of America’s most soulful and culturally rich musical traditions. Enjoy incredible live blues music from some of the region’s most talented artists in a smoke-free atmosphere, with great food and drink specials starting at 8:00 PM.

Since 1996, the Blues Society of Northwest Florida has championed the local Blues scene, supported the International Blues Foundation, and participated in the world-renowned International Blues Challenge in Memphis, TN. Together with Seville Quarter, they are committed to preserving, promoting, and celebrating Blues music in all its forms, from the Mississippi Delta and Chicago, to New Orleans, Kansas City, the Carolinas, Florida, and beyond.

Blue Mondays at Seville Quarter promise a Beale Street, backstage-pass vibe right here in Pensacola—intimate, authentic, and always unforgettable.
